issues.quote: You open `db/seed.sql` to check the prices: it fills the tables with their starting rows, in the order it lists them. The lab is the copy of Đơn Hàng that `scripts/up.sh` starts on your laptop.
issues.text: The lab sentence sits between opening seed.sql and reading the prices, and nothing in the situation has mentioned the lab yet. I stopped to wonder why I was told about it here.
issues.fix: Move the lab sentence into the first paragraph: 'shows you what PostgreSQL printed in the lab, the copy of Đơn Hàng that `scripts/up.sh` starts on your laptop'.

issues.quote: In a query like this one, it may sort by any column of the table, even one `SELECT` does not show
issues.text: 'In a query like this one' makes me ask which queries are different, and the lesson never says. The Suggested answer relies on this rule, so I carry that doubt into the exercise.
issues.fix: Replace 'In a query like this one' with 'In a query that reads one table, like this one'.

issues.quote: Every column in Đơn Hàng's tables has the rule `NOT NULL`: written out on ordinary columns, and implied on each primary key column, so PostgreSQL refuses to store `NULL` in it; this query makes one on purpose.
issues.text: One paragraph covers the third query, AS, the NOT NULL rule and where NULL can appear. I re-read it to see that 'one' in 'makes one on purpose' means a NULL value, not a column or a rule.
issues.fix: Replace 'this query makes one on purpose' with 'the third query writes `NULL` itself, on purpose'.

issues.quote: it asks PostgreSQL two questions about `NULL` directly, `SELECT` prints both answers as one row, and `AS` gives each a column name.
issues.text: `IS NULL` is used here, but the prose never says what it asks until the misconception section ('`IS NULL` asks the opposite'). I only worked out from the `t` in the output that it tests whether a value is NULL.
issues.fix: After 'two questions about `NULL` directly', add: '`NULL = NULL` compares, while `NULL IS NULL` asks whether the value is `NULL` and always answers true or false'.

issues.text: The output opens with '...' and the prose does not say what was cut. I wondered whether I missed a line that matters, and whether my own terminal should show something there.
issues.fix: Add to the sentence before the block: 'the `...` stands for a few set-up lines psql prints first, which this lesson skips'.

issues.quote: The options you can ignore in this lesson pick which PostgreSQL to talk to (the one in the lab), the user to log in as, and which of its named sets of tables to use, skip psql's start-up settings files, and stop at the first error.
issues.text: One sentence lists five options with three verbs (pick, skip, stop); I had to re-read to match each part to an option. All words are understandable; only the length slowed me.
issues.fix: Split after 'to use': '... and which of its named sets of tables to use. Two more skip psql's start-up settings files and stop at the first error.'
